subject: Priv deploy: evidence ownership & operator access (MSA/Order Form)
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@starlitehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Starlite Health Procurement <procurement@starlitehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Priv deploy: evidence ownership & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are progressing internally on the procurement side and legal has a few follow-up asks before we can move the Order Form/MSA to redlines. High level they want:

- A short mapping table that shows which evidence/artifact Redwood will own and which the customer must produce for an on-prem or VPC deployment (snapshots, witnessing, key handback, operator access logs).
- Proposed language we can drop into the MSA (or an annex) that clarifies operator access boundaries and the conditions for "witnessed" verification.
- Confirmation of whether Redwood will entertain an "escrow-lite" arrangement (sealed snapshot + third-party witness) and any lead time or costs.

Procurement also flagged they need an expected timeline for legal review (target: final redlines back to us in 2 weeks) and whether there are pricing or SLA implications for the on-prem evidence path. We can share our SOC2 but legal still wants the attestation workflow spelled out.

Can you send the mapping and a proposed draft of the MSA paragraph? If easier, we can do a 30-min call with Lauren (our counsel) to walk through.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Director, Integrations
Starlite Health

Attachments: Starlite-SOC2-Jun2026.pdf (pdf)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Priv deploy: evidence ownership & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

Hi Marta — really appreciate the clarity. Attaching our "PrivDeploy Evidence Checklist" which maps artifacts and typical ownership model for the three flavors: hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem). See key highlights:

- Redwood-provided artifacts: baseline build manifests, runtime hashes, and operator runbook excerpts.
- Customer-provided artifacts: network attestations, local operator witness availability, and physical access confirmations.
- Escrow-lite option: we can offer a sealed snapshot deposit with an independent third-party witness. That option usually adds a one-time admin fee and ~3 week scheduling window for witnessing and notarization.

Lauren — looping you in for proposed MSA language and any limitations we should call out (territory, transfer of custody). Priyom — FYI on the technical pieces (SAML/SSO, snapshot handling); I attached a SAML diagram that procurement asked about.

Next steps I propose: 1) Legal draft of a short annex we can use as an Order Form exhibit, 2) quick 30-min sync with Starlite legal to answer any open questions, 3) confirm whether procurement wants the escrow-lite quote.

I can be available Wed 11/18 9–11 PT or Thu 11/19 1–4 PT.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: PrivDeploy-Evidence-Checklist.pdf (pdf), SAML-SSO-diagram.png (png), SLA-exhibit-draft.docx (docx)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Priv deploy: evidence ownership & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the checklist and drafted two short options for insert language — one narrow (operational carveout + witness schedule) and one broader (annex addressing custody, escrow-lite, and rollback). Key calls:

- Keep the core MSA language narrow and put process-level details in an annex or Order Form exhibit. That reduces friction for hosted customers.
- For operator access we should require customer acceptance of a scoped operator runbook and a mutually agreed witness window for any snapshot access. We should not commit to unlimited forensic access; language should be "reasonable and limited" and conditioned on compliance with the annex.
- Escrow-lite: we can offer sealed-snapshot deposit with third-party witness; recommend including an explicit fee and scheduling availability clause (e.g., witness events are scheduled at least 21 days in advance).

I attached a redline of the SLA exhibit (simple markup). Priyom, please confirm the technical feasibility of the witness workflow (how we deliver hashed snapshots and auditor access). David — pls advise on whether we need to route this to Revenue Ops for order form pricing guidance.

Proposed timeline: we can deliver a clean annex language by EOD Wed (11/18) and join a 30-min review with Starlite legal on Thu (11/19).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-exhibit-draft.docx (redline)

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@starlitehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Starlite Health Procurement <procurement@starlitehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Priv deploy: evidence ownership & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

Thanks Tessa/Lauren — helpful. Procurement did a quick pass and asked for two clarifications before we take redlines to our legal team:

1) Rollback & continuity: can Redwood commit to a documented rollback procedure if a witnessed validation reveals an incompatibility? If not, we need explicit language about mutual remediation steps and escalation path.

2) Audit window timing: procurement wants a guaranteed 60-day window from signed order for the first witness event (they need to schedule their facilities). Can Redwood commit to a scheduling SLA or is that only best-effort?

On pricing — procurement flagged the escrow-lite fee as acceptable but asked for a not-to-exceed estimate so it can be budgeted into the PO. They also requested any change to the SLA (e.g., availability carveouts during witness) be documented.

I've attached our SOC2 and we've included a short list of internal timing constraints. If you can send the annex + an NTE fee range for the escrow-lite option we can get legal and procurement aligned.

Best,
Marta

Attachment: Starlite-SOC2-Jun2026.pdf (pdf)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Priv deploy: evidence ownership & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

Great — thank you, Marta. Summary of agreed next steps and deliverables:

1) Redwood will deliver a proposed Annex (Order Form Exhibit) that: maps artifact ownership, defines the witnessed-snapshot workflow, and includes a rollback & remediation section. (Deliverable: clean annex language)
2) Redwood legal (Lauren) will provide a short clause for the main MSA that references the annex and limits operator access to a scoped runbook and audit events. (Deliverable: MSA clause)
3) Pricing: Revenue Ops (David) will provide an NTE estimate for the escrow-lite witness event and any SLA carveouts. Expect a ballpark within 24 hours.
4) Scheduling SLA: we can commit to scheduling the first witness event within 60 days of the signed Order Form subject to 21-day advance notice for witness coordination. We will include this as a scheduling SLA in the annex.

I attached the updated checklist plus a draft annex (clean) for initial review. I'll also send a calendar invite for Thu 11/19 2:00 PM PT for a 30-min review with your counsel — link included in HubSpot and the drive folder.

If that all looks good, we will issue the DocuSign packet with the Order Form placeholders and the annex attached so your legal can do an inline redline. HubSpot record: HS-8342.

Thanks — speak soon,
